newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Shekel rises against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Shekel rises against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed slightly higher against the dollar and the basket of key foreign currencies on Tuesday after the Bank of Israel intervened in the local market to support the basket, dealers said.
"Trading was very quiet today. The Bank of Israel had to intervene in local trading after the dollar declined overseas," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"The central bank bought dollars on a relatively high scale but it failed to raise the basket above seven percent below the diagonal rate," she said.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2590 shekels against 3.2620 shekels on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6172 shekels against 3.6192 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7993 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8032 on Monday and against the mark at 2.0562 shekels against 2.0542 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.2600 shekels.
